messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Sev2: repeated GPU OOMs in pool gpu-prefill-prod-3 -> multiple container restarts (6 nodes) detected in last 7m. Model: gptx-13b-v1. Symptom: "CUDA out of memory" during prefill path (long prompts). Possible customer impact: requests failing / timeouts. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prefill-oom. Paging @mike-oncall @jessica

mike-oncall: ack. Jumping in. Reassigning to runtime and SRE. Starting mitigation coordination.

jessica: seeing 18 restarts across nodes [gpu-node-17,gpu-node-18,gpu-node-19]. Crash log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-17T02:10:21Z] runtime ERROR: CUDA OOM on alloc 12.3GiB (requested by prefill_worker thread)
Trace: at runtime/prefill.cc:412 prefill_kv_alloc()
context_tokens=65536 request_size=~1.2MiB
Container restart count: 3 within 2m for gpu-node-17
```
Looks like long-context prefill (>=60k tokens) triggering OOM. Recommend immediate request-size guard at the gateway and route oversized requests to fallback model.

eli: confirmed on runtime side. Root cause likely miscomputed token count for combined system+user prompt in certain encodings, leading to KV cache allocation > expected. I have a hotpatch: enforce PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS and add defensive OOM catch to drop prefill early. Short-term mitigations:
- Apply gateway rule: reject or 413 requests with context_tokens > 32k
- Add routing: oversized -> gptx-7b-quant fallback (coldmodel)
- Cordon/rotate affected nodes if restarts continue

nina: customer impact: Acme Payments (dedicated) reporting ~4% errors, mostly invoices feature. They want ETA.

mike-oncall: plan of action (short):
1) Apply gateway throttle rule for >32k tokens (temporary)
2) Scale up fallback pool (gptx-7b-quant) by +30%
3) Canary deploy runtime hotpatch to canary nodes
4) Cordon gpu-node-17 and drain if restarts persist
5) Notify customer with interim mitigation note (nina)

eli: executing canary now. Commands: 
```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/gpu-runtime PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=32000 && 
kubectl rollout restart deployment/gpu-runtime-canary
```
Pushing patch that checks token_count before KV allocation and returns 413 if over limit.

ops_bot: Canary rollout succeeded (gpu-runtime-canary) in 18s. Health: OK. No OOMs observed on canary nodes in last 2m.

jessica: I ran cordon/drain on gpu-node-17 as precaution: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
Pods rescheduled. Observed container restart rate drop on that node.

mike-oncall: gateway rule applied at edge: requests with context_tokens > 32k now receive 413 + guidance header: X-Redwood-Action: reduce_context or use_fallback. Error rate for Acme profile: 22% -> 3% in 5m.

nina: sent customer update: "We have applied throttles and a fallback routing policy to reduce failed requests. Engineering is rolling a hotfix and we expect service stabilization within 30-45 minutes. Will follow up with full incident summary." (customer acknowledged).

eli: Canary validated. Rolling to prod with canary percent: 10% -> 100% in 10m. Patch includes PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS enforcement and robust OOM handling for prefill path.

jessica: monitoring metrics: GPU memory tail for pool dropped by ~40%, restart count normalized. No new restarts on gpu-node-18/19 after routing rule.

mike-oncall: closing immediate pager. Will open postmortem (assign to runtime + SRE) to cover: token counting bug, lack of prefill guardrails, and improved observability for KV cache allocation.

eli: follow-ups:
- PR queued: runtime: enforce token accounting for multibyte encodings + unit tests (link: https://git.redwood/runtime/pull/4321)
- Gateway improvement: persistent policy to limit prefill tokens by model tier
- Add alert: high restart rate + OOM signature -> automatic temporary routing to fallback

nina: will update customer after postmortem is available.

mike-oncall: thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity -> Sev3 (impact limited). Postmortem link TBD.
